# 18 New AI Tools From Hacker News's Front Page, October 2026

Hacker News's front page is a reasonable filter for what working engineers found worth their time. Between August and October 2026, eighteen AI tools crossed that bar, and they cluster into a clear pattern: the interesting work moved from *making the model better* to *making the loop around the model better*.

Here is what launched, what each one actually does, and where it fits. Every entry below is verified against the project's own published material — no invented pricing, no borrowed benchmarks.

## Coding agents, rethought

[[link:/tools/1574|Ante]] — a self-contained coding agent as a single roughly 15 MB Rust executable with Grep and git compiled in. It supports interactive TUI, headless, server and gateway modes, runs fully offline against local GGUF files, and in the author's own twenty-task container test used about 7x less peak memory than Claude Code. macOS and Linux only, free during beta preview.

[[link:/tools/1570|Whiteboard]] — an open-source canvas for software design where agents draw diagrams through MCP session tools. Built on a customized Code OSS base with an Electron desktop app, it combines prose, code peeks and sequence steps in one reviewable file, and has a batch authoring mode so the same review pipeline runs headless in CI. From Y Combinator's W26 batch.

[[link:/tools/1571|Huzzah]] — an experimental editor that replaces longform chat prompts with persistent, declarative pseudocode files. You write a `.hz` file describing the shape of what you want; each save becomes a diff and the model regenerates the affected source. The author is candid that it suits new codebases better than legacy ones and that cross-file dependencies remain a known gap.

[[link:/tools/1581|Pi pod]] — a self-hosted layer that runs the pi coding agent in isolated sandboxes on your own server, consolidating agent sandboxing, native clients, role-based session sharing and browser automation. Designed to feel identical to an existing pi harness. The hosted service is listed as coming soon.

[[link:/tools/1573|Copperhead]] — described by its authors as a Cursor for circuit boards: an open-source, verification-first AI agent for PCB design. Point it at a KiCad repository and it edits real schematic and layout files, updates every referencing document, and runs KiCad's own ERC and DRC checks until they pass. Eight gated stages from brief to gerbers. CLI is free and Apache-2.0; hosted cloud runs start at $49 per user per month.

[[link:/tools/1580|SolidCraft]] — a parametric 3D CAD application in pure Rust, on desktop, in the browser and through an MCP server with tools for execute, inspect_design, measure and set_parameter. One published build holds 3,323 editable timeline steps that rebuild without errors. Dual MIT or Apache-2.0, and self-described as early but usable for simple parts.

## Agent safety and context

[[link:/tools/1577|OpenAPPA]] — a deterministic guardrail engine that tracks data flow instead of matching patterns. It runs outside the agent's prompt and execution loop, driven by one declarative contract of data sources, audiences, trust levels and authorities. Security labels only ever tighten, and the engine returns remedy plans with sanitizers, authorities and subagents instead of refusing. MIT licensed, backed by a NeurIPS-accepted paper.

[[link:/tools/1578|ai-rete-RAG]] — pairs a Rete rule engine with retrieval-augmented generation so a decision stays deterministic while the explanation stays grounded. Rules decide the what and produce an auditable trace; retrieval narrates the why from your own documents. Eight built-in demo domains, live with no signup.

[[link:/tools/1576|ThoughtDAG]] — an open-source AI conversation canvas that makes context editable instead of invisible. Conversations become a directed graph where each wire is a route into the next request, with a preview of exactly what the model will receive before you send. Ships as a CLI, an MCP server, a DeepSeek Harness plugin and a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux.

[[link:/tools/1586|OzBrain]] — a shared knowledge layer that every AI agent on your team reads and writes, positioned as a company brain rather than another per-product memory. Connect it from the connector menu in Claude or ChatGPT. Knowledge nests into pieces so an agent pulls only the slice it needs, newer thinking automatically supersedes older notes, and every write is recorded with the agent and reason. Free up to 50 articles; Pro $20 per month.

## Models that fit where models usually do not

[[link:/tools/1572|Cactus Needle 3]] — a foundation model shipped as a single 8 to 29 MB binary for phones, wearables, robots and microcontrollers. 29 to 121 million parameters as laddered subnetworks from 2 to 20 layers, handling tool calls, structured extraction and text embeddings at 400 to 4,000 tokens per second on a Raspberry Pi 5. Install with pip and decorate functions to expose them as tools.

[[link:/tools/1575|Slotstream]] — runs AI models too large for your Mac's memory by keeping shared weights resident and streaming mixture-of-experts layers from SSD on demand. A single native Swift binary on MLX and Metal serving Ollama, OpenAI and Anthropic compatible APIs. Targets Apple Silicon Macs with 16 to 64 GB of RAM; a 48 GB machine reports around 21 tokens per second on a 105 GB model. MIT licensed.

[[link:/tools/1582|Mini-AGI]] — a continual learning byte-level language model that assembles its own architecture, trains from scratch on a single 8 GB VRAM GPU and keeps learning from everything it reads. Weights live as ordinary files on disk and page onto the card as needed, so parameter count is bounded by free disk space. The author calls it a small toy-level model rather than a frontier one.

## Search and retrieval

[[link:/tools/1579|Scry]] — a programmable search MCP server that lets an agent run one bounded query across 108 billion indexed rows instead of reading ten web links. Covers Reddit, Hacker News, LessWrong, arXiv, Stack Exchange, Wikipedia and prediction markets. The agent reads the live schema and writes the query itself. Free for non-commercial use when there is capacity; setup takes about two minutes with no code.

## Local-first, on your own hardware

[[link:/tools/1584|SCM]] — short for Screen Memories, a local-first macOS app that runs deep AI search across every photo and every frame of video in any folder. Five modes cover file similarity, scene-level video retrieval, OCR in 36 languages, spoken dialogue and an optional local chat model. No accounts, no cloud, no uploads.

[[link:/tools/1585|BetterWispr]] — a free, open-source dictation app for macOS that transcribes locally with no account and no cloud fallback. Hold Option and Space, speak, and cleaned text lands where your cursor was. Nine built-in speech models across Apple speech, Parakeet and Whisper, plus a notetaker mode using Apple Intelligence or Ollama on your Mac. Apache 2.0 licensed.

## Something genuinely different

[[link:/tools/1583|Stillwet]] — a gallery where AI models write every brushstroke as code and a simulation renders it as oil paint or watercolour, with no image generator involved. Each painting ships with a replayable session and a written journal of what the model decided to change. 109 published paintings, free to browse.

[[link:/tools/1587|MySetup.ai]] — a community directory where engineers and makers publish the AI tools, workflows and harnesses they actually use. Profiles show what someone has tried, what they moved on from and how their stack evolved. Free to browse and share.

## What the pattern says

Four things stand out across all eighteen.

**Verification beat generation.** Copperhead's ERC and DRC gates, SolidCraft's geometry constraints, OpenAPPA's algebraic labels — the strongest launches all put an oracle outside the model. None of them trust the model to check itself.

**Context became a first-class object.** ThoughtDAG's editable graph and OzBrain's shared brain both treat "what the model knows" as something you build and inspect, rather than a side effect of chat history.

**Constraints got small.** A 15 MB agent binary, an 8 to 29 MB model, a dictation app with no cloud. The launches that got attention were the ones that removed dependencies, not the ones that added capability.

**Deterministic replaced probabilistic where it mattered.** Two of the eighteen are explicitly deterministic-by-design, and both are in safety or compliance roles. That is a meaningful shift from the previous wave.

If you only try two: [[link:/tools/1574|Ante]] for the resource profile and offline operation, and [[link:/tools/1576|ThoughtDAG]] because making context visible fixes more "the model forgot" complaints than any prompt change.

## FAQ

**Are these all free?**

No. Several are free and open source, some are freemium, and Copperhead charges $49 per user per month for hosted cloud runs. Each entry above states what the project publishes.

**Which should I try first?**

Depends on your bottleneck. If agents feel slow or heavy, Ante. If the model keeps forgetting or contradicting earlier decisions, ThoughtDAG. If you are about to put an agent in front of real data, OpenAPPA.

**Were these verified?**

Yes. Every fact above — sizes, speeds, prices, platform requirements — comes from the project's own published material or repository. Nothing is estimated or inferred.

**Why these eighteen and not others?**

They are AI tools that appeared on Hacker News's front page between August and October 2026 and that this directory did not already cover. Hardware projects, programming languages and non-AI utilities were left out.
tldr: Eighteen AI tools launched August–October 2026 that made Hacker News's front page, all verified against published material. The pattern: verification beat generation, context became inspectable, and the strong launches removed dependencies rather than adding capability.
